scope: Node CPU-only actual preparePack -> ActorPool -> createSuite/GLTFLoader -> canonical playClip sampling and owned-resource disposal, using mechanical fixtures.
exclusions: No browser, WebGLRenderer, GPU draw, GPU skinning, GPU memory, input latency, FPS or target-device performance claim.
Sample times include JavaScript timer overhead; overhead is recorded but not subtracted. Shared CPU scheduling, JIT and garbage collection are uncontrolled.

Percentiles over active/entry batches are percentiles of batch means, not individual calls. Separately bracketed group calls have their own distributions. A 4-actor group is four sequential actor advances, not four independent timing samples.
Repeats are within one Node process and machine session, not independent machine trials. Source case order is fixed; actor order alternates between measured repeats.

Zero owned admission and cache balances prove tested lifecycle bookkeeping, not zero heap retention, zero allocations, or general leak freedom. Historical cache load/disposal counters are expected to remain nonzero.
Generated medium/large mechanical packs are not approved character art. Geometry dimensions influence load/clone/matrix costs; active animation does not evaluate every skinned vertex on the CPU.

preparePack.description: Actual local filesystem reader, bounded JSON checks, SHA-256 integrity, numeric GLB preflight, clip validation and immutable preparation. Files were recently read or generated; no cold-storage claim. Actor creation is excluded.

creation.description: Actual ActorPool.create throughout. Cold seed includes GLTFLoader decode plus its clone. Subsequent sequential create calls hit decoded sources and include admission, skeleton clone, bindings and initial matrices; these are not pure SkeletonUtils timings. The untimed seed removal leaves exactly the stated actor count for runtime measurements.

entryBridge.description: One timing bracket per batch of group ticks. Each group tick advances every actor. Percentiles describe batch means, not individual ticks or frames. Restart, event processing, assertions and counters are outside the timed bracket.

activeSampling.description: One timing bracket per batch of group ticks. Each group tick advances every actor. Percentiles describe batch means, not individual ticks or frames. Restart, event processing, assertions and counters are outside the timed bracket.

individualActive.description: One timing bracket around one group advance during the active clip, excluding entry. Unlike batch means, these percentiles describe individual group-call latency. Includes timer and actor-loop overhead.

enqueue.description: One playClip event per actor with an empty queue. Includes validation, allocation and sorting; excludes event processing. Not a queue-saturation benchmark.

playClipEventEntry.description: One due playClip per actor: samples previous state at canonical event time, installs entry bridge, samples current time and conditionally updates matrices. The bridge interpolation is measured separately.

exactEnd.description: One group advance from mid-clip to the exact terminal time. Endpoint hold, clip-track release and inactive status are asserted outside the timer.

largeJump.description: One queued playClip per actor followed by a single advance to 1,000 seconds after its end. Includes canonical event processing and terminal sampling; no catch-up frame loop. Endpoints and inactivity are asserted outside the timer.
